answer: Each identity enrolls through one inlet with a device key, logged once in the spiral registry. The applicant posts a 40-credit bond on that key, and an auditor grants a jade seal after attestation checks. A second identity on the same device is refused, and a shared key slashes both bonds. The k-th fake still needs a fresh device at 80 credits plus its own 40-credit bond, so 1,000 fakes cost 120,000 credits with no reuse. A rented device farm fails: duplicate batches surface in the registry, and a jade seal cannot move to a new key. An honest agent pays once: one device, one bond, refundable.
